Comment: Entered a traded into wave 3. Moved the SL to BE and the price kept rising. Moved the TP +1R and moved the SL to 1R. Price lingered around resistance line and fell. Closed the trade at 1.09242

Entered a trade in the beginning of wave 5 on the 4H chart. I dropped to 1H and entered a bit late - 10 candles after Big Shadow in the Asia session. The SL was hit. At the time I entered RSI was overbought and MACD was declining.
Watched the correction go deeper from the former structure. Waited for 6.18 level and dropped to 1H chart. Waited for a trigger and got a Last Kiss a day after. SL was hit and EMA turned bearish.
On Aug 1st moved the SL to BE - the price was flat for three days, indicating the wave 3 is unlikely. And possible descending triangle on the 4H chart. The trade is exited on the BE.

Observed a valid Last Kiss setup following a clear 4H impulse (wave 1) and a deep wave 2 correction that evolved into a prolonged flat, forming a consolidation box. Entry was taken via sell stop after a retouch, but price was still being accepted at the box edge. The retouch candles were conservative and lacked bearish displacement, resulting in a fake-out and stop-loss hit. Two days later, price dropped ~1.5% after an aggressive bearish candle, confirming the directional bias but highlighting that the entry was premature. Key lesson: correct analysis, poor timing — Last Kiss entries require clear rejection and momentum away from the box, not mere retests.

After allowing wave 4 to fully complete on the 4H chart, dropped to 1H and waited for confirmation. A clear bearish Big Shadow formed on Mar 1 at 17:00, showing strong rejection at structure. Entered short via sell stop with SL just above the Big Shadow high and TP at the 1.618 Fibonacci extension, targeting wave 5. Stop was moved to breakeven on Mar 3 per plan. Price followed through impulsively and hit TP on Mar 4. Key takeaway: patience and aggressive candle confirmation turned the same directional bias into a high-quality A+ trade.

After a prior bearish impulse, price entered a corrective phase. An impulse was recognized later once structure became clear. A trendline drawn from the two previous lows aligned with a 4H key level, forming strong confluence. Price was rejected from this area, and a clear bearish Big Shadow formed on the 1H chart on Apr 4 at 18:00. Entered short via sell stop with SL above the Big Shadow. Stop was moved to breakeven on Apr 5 at 22:00 per plan. Price continued lower and hit TP on Apr 8 at 14:00. Key takeaway: patience and structural confluence combined with rejection-based entry produce high-quality outcomes.

Entered short on Apr 24 after identifying a shallow wave-2 correction (~38.2%) following a strong bearish impulse. Fibonacci retracement was drawn correctly, and I waited for confirmation that the correction was complete. A bearish Big Shadow formed on the 1H just below the 0% of wave 1, confirming rejection and continuation. Entered short with SL above the Big Shadow and moved stop to breakeven on Apr 25. Target was based on a 1.618–2.618 extension of wave 1, with awareness of the 1.05406 key level. Position was closed at 1.05505 due to proximity to structure. Outcome: +2.87R. Key takeaway: shallow corrections in strong trends paired with rejection candles provide high-quality continuation entries.

After a completed 5-wave structure, price entered a clear consolidation range. On June 9, strong bearish pressure appeared, signaling potential range resolution. A sell stop was placed on June 10 and activated on breakdown. With a daily key level at 1.05406 nearby, the stop loss was conservatively placed in the middle of the box, and the take-profit was set at 2R rather than an extension target. Price followed through cleanly and hit TP the following day. Outcome: +2.19R. Key takeaway: adapting risk and expectations to consolidation breakouts leads to clean, low-stress profits.

Identified a developing wave 3 in a bearish environment but entered late into the impulse due to hesitation. A Big Shadow formed on July 1 at 14:00, and I entered short with SL and TP placed per plan. However, the entry occurred after significant displacement, and the candle formed inside an extended move rather than at a transition or retest. Price retraced and hit the stop loss. Outcome: -1R. Key takeaway: Big Shadow entries lose effectiveness when taken late in an impulse; better to wait for a corrective retest or skip the trade entirely.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Post-review note: Stop placement was technically correct, but entry occurred late in wave 3. Normal corrective retrace stopped the trade before continuation. Lesson: avoid Big Shadow entries inside extended impulses or widen stop to structural level.

Observed a long wave-4 flat consolidation after a bearish Elliott structure and anticipated a directional resolution due to extended price compression and historical lows. Drew a consolidation box and waited for a breakout followed by a Last Kiss entry. Entered long on Aug 11 after a retouch, with SL placed at the midpoint of the box. Price moved briefly higher but failed and hit the stop loss. Outcome: -1R. Post-review: trade was taken in a neutral market with no higher-timeframe trend or impulse clarity. Last Kiss setup occurred in balance conditions with multiple fake-outs. Key takeaway: avoid breakout trades without clear directional bias and structural imbalance, regardless of perceived “cheap” price.

After an extended consolidation, a valid Moolah formed on the 1H chart. Although the 4H context was still bullish, the structure inside the range supported a potential downside break. On Sep 13 at 14:00, PMI news provided volatility and confirmed the Moolah setup. Entered short via sell stop with reduced risk (0.25%) and a 2R target. Price remained range-bound initially, with readiness to exit if rejected from the bottom of the consolidation box. Eventually, price broke lower and reached TP on Sep 26. Outcome: +2.04R. Key takeaway: valid execution of a B-grade, counter-context range trade; discipline and risk control were correct, but HTF alignment was missing.

Price had been trending lower inside a well-defined descending channel since March. On the 1H chart, price reached the lower channel boundary and began forming a clear 5-wave corrective structure. Entry was planned in wave 5 after signs of exhaustion. On Oct 3 at 03:00, a Big Shadow appeared, followed by another aggressive Big Shadow later in the session, confirming rejection. A buy stop was triggered at 17:00 with SL below structure. Take profit was placed at daily resistance rather than a Fibonacci extension. Price reached the target the next day. Outcome: +2.20R. Key takeaway: counter-trend trades are valid only at HTF extremes with completed structure and strong rejection; structure-based targets outperform projections.

Price broke a descending channel and a daily resistance level on Oct 25. I waited for a retest and entered long after a Big Shadow printed above resistance on Oct 26 at 10:00. A buy stop was triggered at 17:00 with reduced risk (0.25%). However, price failed to show acceptance above the level, with overlapping candles and weak follow-through. The move proved to be a false breakout, and price fell back below resistance, hitting the stop on Oct 28 at 09:00. Outcome: -1R. Key takeaway: breakout Big Shadows require prior acceptance and displacement above the level; without proof of acceptance, Big Shadow signals are unreliable.

During a developing 5-wave structure, I waited for wave 4 to correct toward the 0.382 fib level. Price stalled slightly above the 0.236, and I began looking for long entries. A bullish candle printed on Nov 23 but was skipped due to lack of clean space to the left. A second bullish candle followed, and a buy stop was placed and triggered around midnight, with SL below the Big Shadow and TP at the next daily resistance. Price failed to follow through and stopped out the next day. Post-analysis showed wave 4 was not fully complete, and the move likely extended above wave 3, indicating a misread wave count. Key takeaway: wave clarity and completion are mandatory — fib reactions without structural resolution are insufficient.

Entered a Last Kiss continuation trade after a second retest of a broken 4H resistance level in an overall bullish structure. Price respected the level and did not show acceptance below. Entry was taken on the second touch, stop placed below structural invalidation between daily and 4H levels, and TP set near the next liquidity above. Trade followed continuation logic with clean space and trend alignment. Outcome +2.07R. Execution quality strong; setup aligned with continuation rules.

A Big Shadow was printed at 14:00 on the 4H key area. I entered 2 hours later, after another two bullish candles - I was simply late, didn't decide based on something else. Because of that I put the SL almost below the original Big shadow - on the 4h Key area and TP on the daily resistance. Two days into the trade the SL was moved at BE. On Jul 20 the SL was hit. A signal candle loses validity after 2 candles unless price returns to the level.

Entered a trade after validating the 4H chart that a potential third wave is beginning. Dropped to 1H to look for a trigger and identified a Big shadow at 9:00 right on the 4H EMA. Placed a Buy stop and it was activated at 11:00 just to be closed at 14:00 by an aggressive bearish candle.

Valid system trade based on 1H Big Shadow at 4H EMA, expecting Wave 3 continuation. Entry and risk management followed rules (5.5R setup, -1R loss). Trade failed because higher-timeframe structure was corrective/distribution, not a true Wave 1–2 base. Missed context: overlapping price action, lack of momentum expansion, overhead supply. Execution good, market read slightly off. Lesson: Only take Wave 3 setups when clear HTF impulse (1–2) is confirmed.

Not every EMA rejection is a Wave 3 setup.

Before trading a Wave 3 setup, the higher timeframe must show a clear Wave 1 and Wave 2 structure. If the structure is overlapping or ambiguous, no trade.
Wave 3 begins after structure resolution, not during structural confusion.
